summary: Zhen Liu works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. Liu earned an MA from the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA from Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fan is attested in 2026 as a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yinshun in 1952. He managed the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992) and taught Chien Y. Hsu.

Zhihua Yao works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After completing a PhD under Malcolm David Eckel at Boston University (~1997–2002), Yao served as Professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and Associate Professor at CUHK (~2005).

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Ng earned an MA under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan and a PhD under Robert M. Gimello at the University of Arizona.

Zhiru Shi (born 1964) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. After earning an MA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, Shi taught at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

Zhiyi Yang (born 1979) is a Sinologist who studied at Peking University, Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. Yang held posts at Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, where Cui served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956). He served as director at the Palace Museum from ~1987 to 1991.

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965), he held posts at Peking University (~1965–1978) and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li works in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University and served as a JSPS DC research fellow, both attested in 2015.

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Evangélikus Gimnázium and Eötvös Loránd University (1895–1900), and later taught Lajos Ligeti.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyuto Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and Rektor at CIHTS (1967–1971).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied at Peking University and under Shili Xiong. He held professorships at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1968–1974) and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974–1995).

Zsóka Gelle (born 1967) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna, Gelle held fellowships at ELTE and the Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).
Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1907) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908).

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning doctorates from the University of Tokyo and Waseda University. He was a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University from 1980 to 2013.
Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1901–1914). He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and École Pratique des Hautes Études. He was a researcher at Toyo Bunko (1964–1970) and Professor at the University of Tokyo (1970–1986).
